result:
Admins can now pin and unpin a discussion from its page. The discussions list puts pinned discussions first and shows a Pinned badge. Pin state is stored in the mock API. I did not run tests, lint, or the app, as you asked.

Changes in `apps/react-vite`:

- **Type and mock DB:** `Discussion` gains `pinned: boolean`. The mock `discussion` model gets a `pinned` boolean, which defaults to false for existing entries.
- **Mock API:**
  - New admin-only endpoint `PATCH /discussions/:discussionId/pin` with body `{ pinned }`. It is scoped to the admin's team and returns 404 when the discussion is not found.
  - `GET /discussions` sorts pinned first before paginating, so pinned items lead on page 1 and stay first across pages.
  - New discussions are created with `pinned: false`.
- **Feature code:**
  - `features/discussions/api/pin-discussion.ts` has the fetcher and `usePinDiscussion`. The hook invalidates the discussion queries and shows a "Discussion Pinned" or "Discussion Unpinned" notification.
  - `features/discussions/components/pin-discussion.tsx` is an admin-only button that reads "Pin Discussion" or "Unpin Discussion". It is rendered in `discussion-view.tsx` next to the update button.
  - `discussions-list.tsx` shows a blue "Pinned" badge next to pinned titles.

Two choices you may want to review:

- I restricted the existing `PATCH /discussions/:id` mock handler to write only `title` and `body`. Before, it passed the whole request body through, so a client could have set `pinned` there.
- The pin button shows only to admins through `<Authorization>`. The mock endpoint also enforces the admin check, so the rule holds on the server side too.

I did not add a badge on the discussion page itself, since the request only asked for one on the list.
